tagline: Around Mount Bachelor to a string of lakes the lava made.
intro: Out of Bend, Century Drive climbs steadily into the Deschutes National Forest, past a lava flow that once shoved the river off its course, and on under the cone of Mount Bachelor. Beyond the ski area the byway turns south along the Cascades by Todd, Sparks, Devils, Elk and Lava lakes, and follows the young Deschutes down to Oregon Route 58, 66 miles from town.
The lakes formed behind lava dams and moraines, in old craters and in basins the glaciers dug. In the mid-1960s astronauts trained along this road for the trip to the moon.

moments.title: Sparks Lake
moments.text: What is left of a larger lake, partly filled with sediment and plants. It has no outlet you can see, and its water slips away into crevices along the southwest shore.

moments.title: Devils Lake
moments.text: Green water over a white pumice bottom, so clear and shallow that boats seem to hang in midair. In 1971 a rock from a dome nearby went to the moon with Apollo 15.

moments.title: Lava Lake
moments.text: Lava from Mount Bachelor made it, and a wall of hardened lava still parts it from Little Lava Lake, where the Deschutes starts out as a small creek.

practical: The byway closes beyond Mount Bachelor ski area in winter.
